title: Confederate States of America
capsule: The Confederate States of America was formed on 8 February 1861 when seven Deep South slave states seceded following Abraham Lincoln's election; four more joined after Fort Sumter, and Jefferson Davis was inaugurated as permanent president on 22 February 1862. The Confederacy's declared cause was the preservation of slavery — Confederate Vice President Alexander Stephens called it the "cornerstone" of the new government — and it fielded armies that at times threatened Washington and invaded Pennsylvania before Union industrial and manpower advantages ground them down. General Robert E. Lee's surrender at Appomattox Court House on 9 April 1865 effectively ended organized Confederate resistance, and the government formally dissolved on 5 May 1865 after Davis was captured. Readmission of the former Confederate states required ratification of the 13th Amendment abolishing slavery.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are thoroughly documented through secession ordinances, though effective Confederate control over border regions and Indian Territory fluctuated significantly during the war.
